title: Repeated shallow answers produce recurring coaching gaps

questions.question: How would you make the failure path safer?
questions.intent: Assess correctness reasoning for a failure boundary.

questions.question: How would you demonstrate this behavior?
questions.intent: Assess testing evidence and verification depth.

answers: PRIVACY_SENTINEL_WEAK_8F3C I would change the implementation.
I would improve this part and describe the result.
expected_recurring_issues: Describe how tests or edge cases would verify the change.
Explain the reasoning in more depth.
Name at least one tradeoff behind the decision.

supporting_findings.explanation: The error boundary does not preserve diagnostic context.
supporting_findings.suggestion: Handle only the expected failure and preserve context.

title: Detailed answers demonstrate every interview signal

questions.question: How would you narrow this error boundary?
questions.intent: Assess correctness reasoning for exception handling.

questions.question: How would you separate these responsibilities?
questions.intent: Assess design judgment around a system boundary.

answers: I would catch the specific exception because the correct failure behavior must preserve context; the tradeoff is extra handling, and I would test the happy path plus an edge case. PRIVACY_SENTINEL_STRONG_2A91
I would move the boundary responsibility into a small helper because that design keeps policy explicit; the tradeoff is another abstraction, and I would verify both callers with focused tests.
expected_strengths: Explained the approach with useful detail.
Included a way to verify the change.
Connected the answer to the interviewer’s intent.

supporting_findings.explanation: Distinct decisions are harder to review together.

title: One strong and one weak answer yield developing readiness

questions.question: How would you make this query boundary safer?
questions.intent: Assess security reasoning for untrusted input.

questions.question: How would you improve this helper?

answers: I would use parameter binding because untrusted values must not alter query structure; the tradeoff is driver-specific syntax, and I would verify malicious input plus the normal path. PRIVACY_SENTINEL_MIXED_C71D
I would change the helper and describe the result.
expected_strengths: Explained the approach with useful detail.
Included a way to verify the change.
Connected the answer to the interviewer’s intent.

supporting_findings.explanation: The value can change the structure of the command.
